prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer looks straight down at a floor corner bounded by walls on the upper-left and a cabinet on the lower-left (0.4–0.8 m away), with the wearer's own torso, knees, and outstretched arms in the foreground (0.1–0.7 m) resting on floor planks and subfloor (0.7–1.1 m) that lie within arm's reach alongside a metal scraper (0.6–0.9 m, about 0.2–0.4 m between the two hands). Across frames 1 to 3 the wearer shifts slightly right and pulls both hands closer to the torso, then rotates roughly 90 degrees counter-clockwise in frame 4—bringing the bright white chest and bent knees (0.1–0.4 m) prominently into the lower foreground—before leaning higher in frame 5 as a second person's hand and leg appear at the top-right edge (~1.1 m away, facing the floor rather than looking at the wearer). The wearer's arms, knees, and torso occlude the underlying planks while the wearer's head and almost all of the second person remain out of view beyond the frame edges. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the elevated vertical wall planes and the wearer's raised limbs and knees from the flat horizontal floor beneath them, and weakly outline the scraper's relief in frame 3. However, the map is unreliable where per-frame auto-scaling inverts relative brightness—making the floor in frame 2 look much darker and farther than in frame 1 despite similar distance—and in frame 5 where the scraper and small tools on the right vanish completely into the dark floor gradient.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels only regions belonging to the 'person' class in the foreground (0.1–0.7 m) and at the top-right edge of frame 5 (~1.1 m), leaving the surrounding walls, cabinet, floor planks, subfloor, and hand tools completely unsegmented in black despite their being within the wearer's 0.7 m arm's reach. In frames 1 to 3, the wearer's left arm (left, 0.3–0.7 m), right arm (right, 0.3–0.7 m, ~0.4 m from the left arm), and lower torso/knees (bottom center, 0.1–0.5 m) are visible and shift downward and rightward before rotating counter-clockwise in frame 4, where the torso and knees expand across the bottom foreground and partially occlude the floor below. In frame 5, as the wearer leans back slightly, a yellow/green mask at the top-right edge highlights the newly entered hand and leg of a second person (~1.1 m away and ~0.6 m ahead of the wearer's right hand, mostly out of view above the frame and oriented toward the floor rather than toward the camera wearer), which is harder to spot immediately against the wood and subfloor in RGB alone. However, the instance segmentation is highly unreliable because it fragments the camera wearer's single body into two or three separate 'person' instances (cyan, pink, and brown) that swap colors across frames, and in frame 4 it falsely merges a large patch of wood flooring between the arms into the brown 'person' mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's left and right hands (~0.5–0.7 m from the camera and 0.25–0.5 m apart from each other) against an entirely black background, omitting all scene geometry, floor tools, and yellow body skeletons. Across frames 1 to 3, both hands stay palms-down within arm's reach on the floor planks while shifting from the upper-left/center toward the lower-center as the wearer moves backward and turns slightly right relative to the corner. In frame 4, as the wearer turns counter-clockwise and leans forward, both hands reach toward the top edge of the frame (~0.7 m away, widened to ~0.5 m apart) on either side of the knees, and in frame 5 they retract to the lower half of the image (~0.6 m away, ~0.25 m apart) on the planks and subfloor. This map makes the exact finger articulation, thumb-to-index spread, and wrist orientation of the wearer's two hands much clearer than the RGB image alone. However, it is unreliable for broader spatial understanding because it fails to detect the wearer's visible arms, shoulders, and knees (which are partially self-occluded and truncated by the bottom frame boundary) and completely misses the second person's visible hand at the top-right edge of frame 5 (~1.1 m away, within reach of the upper floor planks and tools).
